lines.text: Three times Paul begged God to take the thorn away.
Three times, heaven said no — and gave him something else instead.
My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
Whatever won't leave you doesn't mean you're forgotten. It means there's room for His power to show up loud.
Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
The thorn stayed. So did He. In Jesus' name, amen.

bold: my strength is made perfect in weakness
title: Word and Faith Network
subtitle: When the Thorn Stays
story: A three-scene illustrated short film on 2 Corinthians 12: a kneeling figure praying beside a wine-dusk thorn bramble that won't move, a single crack of gold light breaking through near-black as the weakness is named honestly, and warm dawn light pouring out over that same thorn as the figure stands with arms raised — grace poured out around what never left.
